## This week

Three parts. Part 1 defines reasoning, intermediate steps before the answer, and the two ways to add it: test-time compute that our prompt and code set in advance, and a reasoning model that writes its own steps and thinks longer on harder problems, which raises accuracy (test-time scaling) on tasks whose answers can be checked. Part 2 is how such a model is trained when no one has written its long solutions: reinforcement learning on the model's own solutions, scored on the final answer only; rewards from a program (RLVR) or from a model of human preferences (RLHF); the reasoning that emerged in DeepSeek-R1-Zero; distillation into smaller models; and the limits of a reward. Part 3 puts a reasoning model into an agent: reasoning effort, interleaved thinking between tool calls, planner and executor, and the faithfulness of its thinking.

## Practice and lab

The practice builds an MCP server of our own. TheMealDB is a public web API of recipes. The server offers two of its requests to a model as tools, a search by ingredient and the recipe of one meal, and it is written in five steps with the MCP Python SDK. The notebook starts the server over stdio, gives its tools to an agent made with `create_agent`, and asks for two meals that use chicken breast and garlic: the agent decides which requests to make and uses the reply of one request in the next. The last part is a discussion task: define the tools of the recipe server again, build one of them, and present it in class. The API needs no key.
